guides.title: Did Proverbs Borrow From Egyptian Wisdom Writing?
guides.blurb: Proverbs sits beside Egyptian instruction. Job and Ecclesiastes answer Babylonian despair. Borrowed forms, and a different God inside them.

guides.title: How Is the Law of Moses Different From Hammurabi?
guides.blurb: Hammurabi's stele and the Torah speak the same legal language. What they say in that language could not be more different.

guides.title: Was Genesis 1 Answering Babylon, Not Modern Science?
guides.blurb: The first chapter of the Bible was answering Babylon, not modern science. Hearing its claims in their own world changes what we ask of them.

guides.title: What Is a Biblical Covenant? The Ancient Treaty Form
guides.blurb: Sinai follows the shape of an ancient treaty between a great king and a rescued people. That shape settles an old argument about law and grace.

guides.title: Why Did Israel's Neighbors Worship Idols?
guides.blurb: Idols were not stupidity. They were a sophisticated technology of presence and control, and the pull they answered has not gone anywhere.

guides.title: Is 'You' in the New Testament Singular or Plural?
guides.blurb: Nearly every 'you' in the epistles is plural, and nearly every reader in the modern West hears it as singular. That one grammatical fact rearranges more than we want it to.

guides.title: What Did Hospitality Mean in the Ancient World?
guides.blurb: In a world without hotels, police, or embassies, the welcome of strangers was the difference between life and death. The Bible treats it accordingly. We have made it a programming word.

guides.title: What Does Clean and Unclean Mean in Leviticus?
guides.blurb: Purity in the Bible is not hygiene and it is not, by itself, sin. It is a map of order and boundary, and you cannot read Leviticus, the Gospels, or Acts 10 without it.

guides.title: What Is Honor and Shame Culture in the Bible?
guides.blurb: The Bible was written in a world where the community's verdict was the heaviest thing a person carried. We read it in a world wired for guilt. The mismatch sits under almost every page.

guides.title: What We Bring to the Text Without Knowing It
guides.blurb: The most powerful assumptions are the ones nobody states. Every reader carries a culture into Scripture, and the Western reader carries one too. The first step is admitting we have an accent.

guides.title: Does the Kingdom of God Belong to a Political Party?
guides.blurb: Jesus refused the Zealots and the Herodians both. Every generation since has tried to draft him anyway, and ours is no exception.

guides.title: Does Your Politics Decide How You Read the Bible?
guides.blurb: Each tribe has a canon within the canon. The verses we underline and the verses we explain away tell the truth about who is actually holding the pen.

guides.title: Is the Bible an American Book? What Its History Shows
guides.blurb: Three languages, a dozen empires, a millennium of authors, and not one of them ever saw a ballot. The text resists every flag we drape over it, including ours.

guides.title: What Does It Mean That Christians Are Exiles?
guides.blurb: Elect exiles, a letter to Babylon, and a refusal in front of a furnace. What changes when the church stops reading like a landlord.

guides.title: What Does Justice Mean in the Bible? Mishpat and Tsedaqah
guides.blurb: Two Hebrew words were doing their work twenty-five centuries before our culture wars. Neither American tribe gets to keep the definition it brought.

guides.title: What Does the Bible Say About Wealth and the Poor?
guides.blurb: Scripture speaks about wealth and the poor with a frequency our preaching has never matched. Both parties found a way to keep the texts and lose the cost.

guides.title: What Happened Between the Old and New Testaments?
guides.blurb: Your Bible has a blank page between Malachi and Matthew. Empires rose and fell on that page, and the world Jesus walked into was built there.

guides.title: What Is the Septuagint, and Why Does It Matter?
guides.blurb: The first churches read their Scriptures in Greek translation, and the New Testament quotes it on nearly every page. Knowing that should steady you, not shake you.

guides.title: What Israel Was Waiting For
guides.blurb: First-century messianic hope was not one expectation but a range of them, and a crucified messiah fit none. That is the point.

guides.title: What Was the Difference Between Temple and Synagogue?
guides.blurb: One building held the presence of God, the national economy, and the politics of an occupied people. Another held the week. You cannot read the Gospels without both.

guides.title: Who the Pharisees Actually Were
guides.blurb: Four movements, one question, and a caricature the church needs to stop repeating.

guides.title: What Are the Household Codes in Ephesians and Colossians?
guides.blurb: Ephesians and Colossians address wives, husbands, children, and slaves in a form Aristotle would have recognized. The form is familiar. The content keeps breaking it.

guides.title: What Did Gospel and Lord Mean Under Caesar?
guides.blurb: The vocabulary of Christian confession was in public circulation before the church ever used it, and the man it pointed to lived in Rome.

guides.title: What Did Grace Mean in a World Built on Patronage?
guides.blurb: Before grace was a doctrine, charis was a word for what benefactors gave and what recipients owed. Paul knew the system. He also broke it.

guides.title: Which Cities Did Paul Write To? Corinth, Ephesus, Rome
guides.blurb: Paul's letters have street addresses. Corinth, Ephesus, Philippi, Rome. Knowing the city explains why each letter worries about what it worries about.

guides.title: Why Was Crucifixion So Shameful in the Roman World?
guides.blurb: In polite Roman society the cross was an obscenity, not a symbol. The first Christians preached it anyway.

guides.title: Did the Gospels Get Jesus Right?
guides.blurb: The telephone game needs long chains, anonymous links, and nobody checking. The Gospels grew up under different conditions, named witnesses, short decades, and communities that could call a storyteller a liar.

guides.title: How Did the Bible Treat Women Compared to Its World?
guides.blurb: Set the biblical texts about women beside Athens, Rome, and Babylon, and something unexpected happens. The book so often accused of diminishing women keeps lifting them past their world. Not past every question. Past their world.

guides.title: Were Ancient People Gullible About Miracles?
guides.blurb: The claim that ancient people would believe anything is itself a belief, held against the evidence. They knew exactly what death was. That is why the resurrection startled them first.

guides.title: What Does the Bible Actually Say About Slavery?
guides.blurb: Abolitionists and slaveholders carried the same Bible into the same century, and only one of them read it whole. What the texts regulated, what they outlawed, and how the church chose not to know.

guides.title: Why Is the Old Testament So Violent? An Honest Look
guides.blurb: The conquest chapters are in the book, and the skeptic who refuses to look away is reading more honestly than the churchgoer who skips them. The hardest ground in Scripture, walked slowly.
